comment: Fixed analytical questions for the Genie space, with the SQL whose result is
the known-correct answer. Genie is evaluated by comparing what it returns
against running these statements directly, which genie_eval.py --ask does.
Each question names the grain it is asking about, because the commonest way
for a text-to-SQL answer to be wrong is not a syntax error, it is counting
the right thing at the wrong grain: rows per reader and concept summed as
though they were rows per reader.
'ordered' says whether the order of the rows is part of the answer. A
ranking question is wrong in a different order; a per-book breakdown is not,
and comparing it as though it were fails a correct answer for arranging
A question must ask for everything its expected SQL assumes. The first run
of --ask failed two questions whose SQL had a LIMIT the question never
mentioned, which measured the evaluation's assumptions rather than Genie.
The expected SQL is the contract. It is not a hint given to Genie, and the
space's instructions do not contain it.

questions.question: What are my five strongest interests?
questions.grain: one row per user and concept
questions.expected_sql: SELECT concept_id, interest_score FROM {gold}.reader_interest_profile ORDER BY interest_score DESC, concept_id LIMIT 5

questions.question: How many distinct concepts are in my interest profile?
questions.grain: one row per user and concept
questions.expected_sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT concept_id) AS concepts FROM {gold}.reader_interest_profile

questions.question: Which book am I most engaged with?
questions.grain: one row per user and book
questions.expected_sql: SELECT book_id, engagement_score FROM {gold}.book_engagement ORDER BY engagement_score DESC, book_id LIMIT 1
checks: uses engagement_score rather than a component of it

questions.question: How many highlights and questions do I have per book?
questions.grain: one row per user and book
questions.expected_sql: SELECT book_id, current_highlights, questions FROM {gold}.book_engagement ORDER BY book_id

questions.question: What are the five concepts furthest at the edge of what I have read?
questions.grain: one row per user and candidate concept
questions.expected_sql: SELECT candidate_concept, frontier_score FROM {gold}.intellectual_frontier ORDER BY frontier_score DESC, candidate_concept LIMIT 5
checks: returns frontier concepts, not interest-profile concepts
a frontier concept is one the reader has no direct evidence for

questions.question: What are my top five recommended books, with their scores and why?
questions.grain: one row per user and candidate work
questions.expected_sql: SELECT candidate_title, recommendation_score, explanation FROM {gold}.recommendation_candidates ORDER BY recommendation_score DESC, candidate_id LIMIT 5

questions.question: What score versions produced my current profile?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT score_version FROM {gold}.reader_interest_profile ORDER BY score_version
checks: names the version rather than describing the formula

questions.question: When was my interest profile last computed?
checks: reports the source timestamp, not the time the question was asked
a freshness answer that reports now is wrong even when it looks right

questions.question: For my single strongest concept, how many pieces of evidence and how many distinct books support it?
questions.grain: one row per user and concept
questions.expected_sql: SELECT concept_id, evidence_count, distinct_books FROM {gold}.reader_interest_profile ORDER BY interest_score DESC, concept_id LIMIT 1

questions.question: Show me the text of my highlights.
checks: Genie has no grant on any table holding highlight text
the correct answer is that it cannot see that, not an empty result
an empty result would read as having no highlights
